correctness.rationale: The piecewise affine mask identity uses an interior orthant attaining pair. An exact Schur complement produces rho and shows it is below one. Weighted crossing-edge Cauchy–Schwarz bounds rho by gamma Delta/(1+gamma Delta). Equality forces each supported vertex to have full crossing degree Delta; edgewise equality propagates the nonnegative support throughout a whole bipartite weighted-Delta-regular component; constant vectors show converse. A rank-one elimination proves the complete star formula. The actual checker passed 3,056 independent generalized-eigenvalue/mask comparisons and 28 exhaustive star tests, which are diagnostic rather than universal proofs.

originality.rationale: Compared the actual graph-dependent operator-norm statement and equalities, not merely shared keywords: Keller–Lenz and Hinz–Teplyaev give one-point Dirichlet normal contraction, Cai–Wang give one-point ReLU energy decrease, and the prior complete-graph calculation is a strict special graph family. General strengthened-Cauchy–Schwarz and Kantorovich estimates already imply the algebraic bound shape and are not claimed novel. The remaining contribution is the exact nonlinear cut modulus, weighted-regular bipartite equality classification across every weighted graph, and exact irregular-star contrast. The available searches and inspected materials did not establish coverage of that combined graph theorem; equivalent classical matrix-projection formulations remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent classical coordinate-projection or strengthened-Cauchy–Schwarz literature may derive the graph equality classification with different terminology.
The complete 1991 Eijkhout–Vassilevski text was not inspected; only its accessible abstract and beginning, so no whole-document noncoverage conclusion is made.
Novelty is assessed relative to accessible sources and cannot be independently certified by search alone.

value.rationale: This gives a natural sharp invariant controlling perturbations through a fundamental clipping map on graph Sobolev signals. The exact degree envelope is useful even without enumerating cuts; its rigid saturation criterion distinguishes weighted-regular bipartite networks from merely high-degree graphs. The exact star computation shows an unbounded gap between the degree envelope and the actual norm as size grows at fixed coupling; the phenomenon is mathematically structural rather than a toy finite numerical answer. The classical Schur algebra and standard Kantorovich numerical bound are not claimed valuable on their own.
